key_terms.meaning: A unit vector in ℂ²: |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ with |α|² + |β|² = 1.
A classical bit has one definite value, 0 or 1; a qubit can be in a complex superposition.
A number z = a + ib, where a and b are real and i² = −1.
A set V with vector addition and scalar multiplication by ℂ satisfying the vector-space axioms.
Vectors v₁, …, vₙ are independent if c₁v₁ + ⋯ + cₙvₙ = 0 forces every cᵢ = 0.
A linearly independent set of vectors that spans the space; every vector has a unique coordinate list.
A map ⟨u|v⟩ to ℂ with conjugate symmetry, linearity, and positivity ⟨v|v⟩ ≥ 0, equal to 0 only for v = 0.
A complete complex vector space with an inner product.
|ψ⟩ denotes a vector, ⟨ψ| its dual, and ⟨φ|ψ⟩ their inner product.
A basis with ⟨i|j⟩ = δ_ij, where δ_ij = 1 if i = j and 0 otherwise.
A map A: V → V satisfying A(αu + βv) = αAu + βAv for all complex α, β.
In a basis {|i⟩}, the entries of A are A_ij = ⟨i|A|j⟩.
A nonzero |v⟩ with A|v⟩ = λ|v⟩; λ is the eigenvalue and |v⟩ the eigenvector.
A matrix with A† = A; its eigenvalues are real and eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal.
A matrix with U†U = I; it preserves inner products and norms.
A construction V⊗W with dimension (dim V)(dim W) and product basis |i⟩⊗|j⟩.
For diagonalizable A = Σᵢ λᵢ|i⟩⟨i|, define f(A) = Σᵢ f(λᵢ)|i⟩⟨i|.
e^A = Σ_{n=0}^{∞} Aⁿ/n!; for Hermitian H, e^{−iHt} is unitary.

takeaways: Quantum computing is a different model of information, not a faster version of the same classical model.
A qubit is a unit vector in a complex Hilbert space, and its amplitudes are complex numbers.
Dirac notation writes vectors, dual vectors, and inner products without matrix indices.
A linear operator is a matrix only after a basis is chosen.
Hermitian operators have real eigenvalues and describe observables.
Unitary operators preserve inner products and describe reversible gates and closed time evolution.
The tensor product builds multi-part state spaces and allows entangled states that are not product states.
Functions of an operator act on eigenvalues, and the matrix exponential turns a Hermitian Hamiltonian into a unitary evolution.
The history of quantum computing shows both the promise of quantum algorithms and the difficulty of controlling quantum coherence.
bank_note: Long answers are expected to connect the linear-algebra definitions to quantum use: Dirac notation, Hermitian versus unitary operators, tensor products, and the historical reason quantum information is hard to control.

bank.q: Define a Hilbert space. Explain why an inner product is needed and write the inner product in Dirac notation.
outline: Complex vector space with inner product
Inner product properties: conjugate symmetry, linearity, positivity
Completeness of the space
Dirac notation: ⟨φ|ψ⟩ and bra as dual vector
Norm and orthogonality

bank.q: Distinguish Hermitian and unitary matrices. Give one physical role of each in quantum computation.
outline: Definitions A† = A and U†U = I
Hermitian: real eigenvalues, orthonormal eigenbasis, observables
Unitary: eigenvalues of modulus one, preserves inner products, gates and time evolution
Examples: Pauli X is Hermitian and unitary; Hadamard is unitary

bank.q: List the axioms of a vector space over the complex numbers and explain what a basis is.
outline: Closure under addition and complex scalar multiplication
Associativity and commutativity of addition
Zero vector and additive inverse
Distributive laws and 1v = v
Basis: independent and spanning; dimension and coordinates

bank.q: Explain the tensor product of two complex vector spaces. State its dimension and give a product basis.
outline: Bilinear product of vectors from V and W
Dimension of V⊗W is (dim V)(dim W)
Product basis |i⟩⊗|j⟩
Inner product factorizes on product vectors
Not every vector in V⊗W is a product vector

bank.q: How is a function f(A) of a diagonalizable operator A defined? Give the condition for f(A) to be Hermitian or unitary when f is real or has modulus one.
outline: Spectral decomposition A = Σᵢ λᵢ|i⟩⟨i|
Definition f(A) = Σᵢ f(λᵢ)|i⟩⟨i|
Real f(λᵢ) gives Hermitian f(A)
|f(λᵢ)| = 1 gives unitary f(A)
Matrix exponential as an example

bank.q: Outline the main historical stages that led from classical computation to quantum computation. Why did the idea look both valuable and difficult?
outline: Classical bit and classical computation model
Quantum mechanics and state description
Feynman's suggestion to simulate quantum systems with quantum systems
Algorithms showing speedups, such as Shor and Grover
Experimental control of qubits and decoherence
Error correction and current limitations

bank.q: For A = [[2, 1−i],[1+i, 3]], show A is Hermitian and find its eigenvalues.
outline: Check A† = A using conjugate transpose
Diagonal entries are real; off-diagonal entries are conjugates
Characteristic equation (2−λ)(3−λ) − (1−i)(1+i) = 0
Eigenvalues λ = 1 and λ = 4

bank.q: Show that U(θ) = [[cos θ, −sin θ],[sin θ, cos θ]] is unitary. Find U(θ)|0⟩ and state the measurement probabilities in the computational basis.
outline: Compute U†U = I
U is real orthogonal, hence unitary
U(θ)|0⟩ = cos θ|0⟩ + sin θ|1⟩
Probabilities are cos²θ for 0 and sin²θ for 1
Angles are real, so probabilities sum to 1

bank.q: Compute the tensor products |0⟩⊗|1⟩ and (|0⟩⊗|0⟩ + |1⟩⊗|1⟩)/√2. Test whether the second state is a product state.
outline: Use basis order |00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩, |11⟩
Bell state has amplitudes 1/√2 on |00⟩ and |11⟩
Assume a product state and compare coefficients
The Bell state is entangled, not a product state

bank.q: Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Pauli matrix X. Use them to compute e^{iθX}.
outline: Eigenvalues +1 and −1
Spectral decomposition X = |+⟩⟨+| − |−⟩⟨−|
e^{iθX} = cos θ I + i sin θ X

bank.q: Given H = [[1,0],[0,−1]], compute e^{−iHt} and verify it is unitary. Interpret the result as time evolution.
outline: H is diagonal and Hermitian
e^{−iHt} = diag(e^{−it}, e^{it})
Conjugate transpose gives the inverse
Each diagonal entry has modulus 1
Relative phase between |0⟩ and |1⟩ changes with time

bank.q: Why is the tensor product, rather than the Cartesian product, the correct construction for composite quantum systems? Discuss with an entangled state.
outline: Cartesian product treats pairs without superposing across parts
Tensor product is bilinear and gives the product basis
Dimension multiplies: dim(V⊗W) = (dim V)(dim W)
Inner products factorize on product vectors
Entangled state such as (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2 is not a product state
Composite measurement correlations follow from the tensor-product structure

bank.q: Compare a classical bit with a qubit. Which claimed advantages of quantum computing follow from the state space and which require algorithms and error correction?
outline: Classical bit has one definite value; qubit is a unit vector in ℂ²
Measurement gives probabilities from amplitudes
Superposition is not parallel classical computation by itself
Interference and entanglement are resources in algorithms
Algorithms such as Shor and Grover give specific speedups
Decoherence and gate errors require error correction
Quantum computing is not a universal speedup for every problem

bank.q: Explain how Hermitian and unitary operators enter the postulates of quantum mechanics. Why does measurement use Hermitian operators and time evolution use unitary operators?
outline: States are unit vectors in a Hilbert space
Observables are Hermitian operators with real eigenvalues
Orthonormal eigenbasis and Born rule for probabilities
Unitary operators preserve norms and inner products
Closed time evolution is unitary, e^{−iHt} for Hermitian H
Measurement is non-unitary and changes the state
Hermitian spectrum matches real measurement outcomes

glossary.def: A complex coefficient in a superposition whose squared modulus gives a probability.
A linearly independent set of vectors that spans the space, so every vector has a unique coordinate list.
The dual vector ⟨ψ| that acts on kets to produce inner products.
A vector |ψ⟩ in a complex Hilbert space.
A metric space in which every Cauchy sequence converges to a point in the space.
For z = a + ib, the number z* = a − ib.
The transpose of a matrix followed by complex conjugation, written A†.
The number of vectors in any basis of a vector space.
A linear functional on a vector space; in Dirac notation it is a bra.
A scalar λ such that A|v⟩ = λ|v⟩ for some nonzero vector |v⟩.
A nonzero vector |v⟩ whose direction is unchanged by A up to the scalar factor λ.
A property of a composite state that cannot be written as a tensor product of states of the parts.
An operator equal to its conjugate transpose, A† = A; it has real eigenvalues.
A complete complex vector space with an inner product.
A map ⟨u|v⟩ to ℂ that is conjugate-symmetric, linear in one argument, and positive definite.
A map A on a vector space that satisfies A(αu + βv) = αAu + βAv.
The series e^A = Σ_{n=0}^{∞} Aⁿ/n!, defined for square matrices.
The length of a vector, ||ψ|| = √⟨ψ|ψ⟩.
A basis whose vectors satisfy ⟨i|j⟩ = δ_ij.
The three standard 2×2 Hermitian and unitary matrices X, Y, Z used to describe one qubit.
A quantum two-level system whose pure state is a unit vector in ℂ².
The set of eigenvalues of an operator.
A construction that combines vector spaces V and W into V⊗W of dimension (dim V)(dim W).
An operator satisfying U†U = I; it preserves inner products and norms.
A Hermitian operator whose eigenvalues are the possible outcomes of a measurement.
A state written as a complex linear combination of basis states.
